subject: Discovery call — data controls & logging requirements

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery call — data controls & logging requirements

Hi Erin —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side so we have alignment and an explicit list of next steps. Please correct anything I missed.

What we heard (pain points):
- Support logs and model request traces currently contain PII (customer names, emails, account numbers).
- Legal requires the ability to redact or not persist PII outside their systems; retention windows differ per data type.
- Auditability: FinFrame needs immutable audit logs that show who accessed what (tenant id + request id) and when.
- Searchability: Security wants logs to be searchable by tenant id and request id for incident response.

Current stack you described:
- In-house app + Snowflake for analytics; Datadog for application logs; using an S3 bucket for longer-term archives.
- KMS is AWS KMS with customer-managed keys for most services.

Success criteria (what would make this a go):
- No PII persisted outside FinFrame-managed storage by default (or configurable redaction).
- Ability to enforce a 90-day retention window for request logs with automated deletion (longer for aggregated metrics).
- Per-tenant audit trails and exportable deletion proof for compliance.
- Option for Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or dedicated capacity to meet isolation/KMS requirements.

Immediate next steps (agreed):
1) I’ll share a short FAQ on how Redwood handles PII, redaction, and retention (attached).
2) Monica will prepare a sample log schema showing which fields we can redact vs. hash vs. keep.
3) Schedule a 30–45 minute compliance call including your security lead (security@finframe.com) to walk through KMS, audit logs, and deletion workflows — Ben to propose times.
4) If we align on controls, we’ll produce a scoped configuration & pricing note for Dedicated/Private options.

Attachments: Redwood-PII-Controls-FAQ.pdf, FinFrame_logs_sample_schema.csv (Monica will tailor).

Thanks — I’ll propose 3 slots in a follow-up.

—

Ben —

This is great, thank you. A few clarifying items from our side before the compliance call:

- Retention: For anything that contains PII we need a default 90-day retention, with the ability to extend to 2 years for aggregated metrics only.
- Deletion proof: Legal requires a deletion proof artifact (timestamp + hash) when data is purged.
- KMS: We use CMKs in AWS KMS and need proof of key separation (we don’t want shared key material with other tenants).
- Searchability: Incident response requires quick search by tenant_id + request_id — but queries must not reconstruct raw PII.
- Redaction: We prefer client-side redaction where feasible; for server-side we need an auditable pipeline.

Security wants to join the call. Possible times (PST): Wed 23 Jun 09:00–11:00, Thu 24 Jun 13:00–15:00, or Fri 25 Jun 08:30–10:00. Please pick one and share an invite (in-person link + dial-in).

Also please send SOC2 type II summary and any relevant encryption docs ahead of the call.

Thanks,
